mathgap.title: Initial counts from 'has' statements
mathgap.principle: Treat statements of the form 'X has N potatoes' as the initial count of X before any transfers or other operations; they are not the final count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a plain count statement appears, record it as the starting value for that person.
mathgap.example: Using the count from 'Myles has 15 oranges' as the final amount after transfers, ignoring later give/take actions.

mathgap.title: Apply transfers correctly
mathgap.principle: For each 'X gives K potatoes to Y' statement, subtract K from X's current count and add K to Y's current count, updating both sides.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a transfer statement, adjust both giver and receiver counts accordingly.
mathgap.example: Failing to subtract K from X or add K to Y, leaving the total number of potatoes unchanged.

mathgap.title: Direct comparison 'has K more than'
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'X has K more potatoes than Y' as the equation X = Y + K, establishing a directed difference.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a direct comparison phrase.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'Taylor has 5 more oranges than Adolfo' as Taylor = Adolfo - 5.

mathgap.title: Absolute difference for 'difference between'
mathgap.principle: Treat 'the difference between the number of potatoes that A and B have' as the absolute value |A − B|, not a signed difference.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement references the difference between two quantities.
mathgap.example: Using A − B directly instead of |A − B|.

mathgap.title: Magnitude interpretation for 'has more than' in equality statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'The number of potatoes that X has more than Y is equal to the difference between A and B', interpret X − Y (a positive magnitude) as equal to |A − B|.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a 'has more than' phrase appears inside an equality.
mathgap.example: Ignoring the magnitude and writing X = Y + (A − B) without taking the absolute value of the right‑hand side.

mathgap.title: Propagate known absolute differences
mathgap.principle: When a statement fixes an absolute difference (e.g., 'X has 9 more than Y'), propagate that as a fixed |X − Y| = 9, allowing you to deduce possible values for X and Y.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After extracting an absolute difference, use it to constrain related variables.
mathgap.example: Failing to enforce that |X − Y| = 9, leading to inconsistent solutions.

mathgap.title: Symbolic substitution over guessing
mathgap.principle: Set up a system of equations for all variables and solve them algebraically; avoid guessing specific values before the system is fully expressed.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When multiple constraints involve the same variables, use substitution rather than trial values.
mathgap.example: Guessing that X = 5 without solving the equations, leading to contradictions later.

mathgap.title: Final consistency check
mathgap.principle: After obtaining a solution, verify that every original statement (including direction of inequalities and transfers) holds true for the derived values.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving the system, before outputting the answer.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution that violates a transfer statement such as 'Robert gives 3 oranges to Myles'.

mathgap.title: Use integer bounds to prune solutions
mathgap.principle: All counts are small non‑negative integers (typically 0‑30) and the answer lies between 10‑30; discard any solution that falls outside these bounds.
mathgap.when_to_apply: During solving, eliminate candidate values that violate the known range.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution where a person's count is 45, which exceeds the allowed range.

mathgap.title: Interpret 'increase by K times' correctly
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'The number of X has increases by K times', compute the new amount as the original amount plus K times the original amount, i.e., new = old * (1 + K). This captures the intended proportional increase rather than a simple multiplication or addition.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever an 'increase by' phrase appears, before setting up equations or solving.
mathgap.example: Treating 'increase by 2 times' as new = old * 2 or new = old + 2, instead of new = old + 2·old.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has' statements as final counts after transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes the given count is the final amount, overlooking later transfer actions.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Record 'has' counts as initial values and apply subsequent transfer statements to update them.

mathgap.description: Interpreting 'has K more than' as X = Y - K
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model reverses the direction of the difference.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Remember that 'X has K more than Y' means X = Y + K.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model interprets the phrase as A - B rather than |A - B|.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always take the absolute value when a statement mentions 'difference between'.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the effect of transfer statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model overlooks that transfers change both giver and receiver counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer by subtracting from the giver and adding to the receiver.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase is ambiguous; the model may default to simple multiplication or addition.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Compute the new amount as old + K·old = old × (1 + K).
